title: The Rulebook Look
description: The app now comes in two looks, switchable under Settings. Rulebook is the new one: aged parchment, heavy black ink, blackletter titles and the blood red of the 1999 book. Grimdark, the black-and-orange theme, is unchanged and still there. The centrepiece is the profile block — every statline is now the rulebook's own M WS BS S T W I A Ld table, framed in ink, wherever it appears: rosters, model pages, the battle reference and shared warbands. The numbers line up in proper columns and can be typed into directly on detail screens, with racial maximums on the row beneath.

title: Opening a Warband by Link No Longer Bounces
description: Refreshing a roster page, bookmarking one, or following a link straight into a warband threw you back to the warband list. The app couldn't tell "this warband doesn't exist" from "we haven't loaded it yet", so it gave up a fraction of a second too early. Every screen behind a warband — roster, models, henchmen, trading, both battle screens, the post-battle sequence and the recruit pages — now waits for the answer.

title: Explore Mordheim From the Wizard
description: The Income step no longer asks how much wyrdstone you found — it rolls for it. The app counts the dice you're owed (one per Hero who came through without going out of action, plus one for a win) and you can add more for skills or equipment. Rolled real dice at the table? Tap any die and set it to what you actually threw; the same works for an Elf Ranger's +1/-1 or a re-roll. Roll more than six and you choose which six count. Doubles and up are looked up for you, including the ones your warband resolves differently — Skaven sell the Straggler, Witch Hunters seal the Graveyard rather than loot it. Gold and shards are added straight to the warband. Anything the app can't do for you, like gaining a Zombie or a wardog, is written into the battle notes, and results that matter next game are added to your warband's notes.

title: A Rulebook Theme, and a New Icon
description: Settings now has an Appearance section with two looks. Grimdark is the dark one you already know. Rulebook turns the whole app into aged paper and black ink with a serif face, closer to reading the printed book — handy under bright light, where a dark screen is hardest to read. Your choice is remembered per device, so your phone at the game store and your laptop at home can differ. The app also has a proper icon now when you add it to your home screen.

title: Save When You're Ready, and Rules That Work Offline
description: Editing a characteristic used to save on every keystroke — one write per digit, with no way to change your mind. Typed fields on the roster, hero, henchmen and campaign screens are now yours until you press Save, with a bar that appears only when something is pending and a Discard next to it. Buying, recruiting, selling and deleting still take effect straight away, because those already are the decision. The rules are also readable without a connection now: once you've opened the app on a device, the full Rules Reference stays available at the table even with no signal. A new version still takes effect the moment you're back online — the old problem of a stale app sticking around cannot happen again.

title: Laid Out Like the Book
description: The Trading Post and your treasury now group gear the way the price chart does — Hand-to-hand Combat Weapons, Missile Weapons, Armour, Miscellaneous — instead of one long list. Henchmen are listed out individually under their group, so four Swordsmen read as four models rather than a multiplier, and their Experience now says "each" because that is how it works. The Rules Reference opens as a chapter list you can expand and collapse, with the number of entries in each; searching still shows a flat list of matches. The Exploration chart is in there too — all 30 results, the wyrdstone shards table and the magical artefacts table.

title: Pick Your Opponent From the Campaign
description: Before a battle you can now choose any warband entered in your campaign as the opponent, not just your own, and their roster is available for reference during the game. Casualties are the big one: tap a Hero out of action, or count how many of a henchmen group went down, and those numbers are waiting for you in the post-battle Injuries step instead of being re-entered from memory afterwards. Stepping the turn counter back now asks first.

title: Advances Follow the Experience Track
description: The post-battle Advances step used to offer an advance to anyone who gained a single point of Experience, which is why it handed out far more than a campaign should. It now counts how many Experience boxes a warrior actually crossed, and each card says how many advances are still to record. Characteristics at their racial maximum can no longer be raised — the old warning triangle looked serious but applied the increase anyway — and rolling one that's already maxed now tells you to roll again, as the rulebook says. Made a mistake? Every recorded advance can be tapped away, instead of restarting the whole wizard. Dead warriors no longer collect Experience or advances, and "That Lad's Got Talent" can finally be recorded: the promoted henchman leaves his group and joins your Heroes with his characteristics and Experience intact.

title: Recruiting Follows the Rules (and Costs Gold)
description: Heroes and henchmen now cost gold when you recruit them, and the warband's maximum size is respected — a henchmen group could previously be sized straight past it. Units you've filled up are greyed out instead of silently accepting more. Hired Swords can finally be hired, with their fee, upkeep, stats and special rules shown before you commit, and they correctly don't take up a warband slot. Every warrior now starts with the free dagger the rules give them, and each unit arrives carrying its own special rules from the book — Leader, Large, Ranger and the rest — instead of a blank card. Warbands are listed A–Z with their source and grade. One rating bug fixed: a henchmen group's Experience counted once for the whole group instead of once per model, so five veterans with 4 XP each scored 29 instead of 45.

title: Browse Public Warbands Without an Account
description: Warbands that players have marked public can now be viewed by anyone, no sign-in needed — so you can send someone a link to your roster and they can actually read it. Find them under "Browse Public Warbands" on the home page. Campaigns changed too: the join-code field is always visible now instead of hidden away, so joining a second campaign is straightforward, and the app no longer invents a campaign called "My Campaign" behind your back the first time you finish a battle. Battles fought outside a campaign are kept as your own.

title: Updates Arrive Straight Away
description: The app used to keep a copy of itself on your device, which meant a new version could sit there unnoticed while the old one kept loading — you'd have had to clear your browser data to see changes. That copy is gone, so you always get the current version. Adding the app to your home screen still works exactly as before. The app has needed an internet connection since accounts arrived, so there was nothing to gain by keeping it.

title: Browse Other Players' Warbands
description: Warbands you mark public now have somewhere to be seen. The Warbands tab has a Public view listing every shared warband with its player, type and rating — search by any of those, filter by warband type, and tap through to a read-only roster. Mark your own warband public from its roster screen, under Campaign & Sharing. Warband types also now read properly everywhere: "Cult of the Possessed" instead of "cult-of-the-possessed".

title: Buying Things Actually Works Now
description: Buying two items in a row could fail with a false "changed elsewhere" warning, and only the first purchase would stick. Saves are now queued so a run of purchases, stat edits, or gold changes all land in order. Number fields across the app — henchmen group size, sell and purchase prices, characteristics, wyrdstone, casualty counts — can now be cleared and typed into properly instead of snapping back to a minimum the moment you empty them. The Standings table also lists every player in the campaign, including the leader and anyone who hasn't entered a warband yet.

title: Play a Campaign Together
description: Campaigns can now have more than one player. Start one and you get a join code like MRDH-7F2K to share — send it straight to WhatsApp, or copy a ready-to-paste message for Discord. Anyone who enters it joins your campaign, and you can issue a fresh code at any time to stop further joins. Enter a warband from its roster screen and it appears in the Standings table alongside everyone else's, with ratings and win/loss records, and you can open any campaign-mate's roster to see their warriors, gear, and skills. Your Border Town Burning objectives stay secret — nobody else can see them, even for a warband you've shared. Paste a code under Campaign, then Players.

title: Sign In From the Menu, and Reset a Forgotten Password
description: The navigation now has a Sign in / Sign out button, so you don't have to dig through Settings to switch accounts. Forgotten your password? There's a link on the sign-in screen — enter your email and we'll send you a link to set a new one. The separate Skills tab is gone, but nothing was lost: all 133 skills are still in the Rules Reference under Skills, grouped by list.

title: The Rules Are Free to Browse
description: You no longer need an account to read the rules. The home page, the full Rules Reference, and every skill list are open to everyone, so you can look something up at the table without signing in. An account is still needed for your own warbands, battles, trading, and campaign log.

title: Accounts & Multi-Device Sync
description: Your warbands now live in an online database behind an email-and-password account instead of being stored in one browser. The same campaign follows you between phone, tablet, and desktop, and clearing your browser no longer wipes everything. Heads-up: warbands you created before this change were stored only on your device and don't carry over automatically — if you still have them in the old browser, export a backup from Settings first, then import it once you've signed in. The app now needs an internet connection to show or change your data.

title: Five More Warbands
description: Added Averlanders, Beastmen Raiders, Carnival of Chaos, Dwarf Treasure Hunters, and Kislevites, bringing the roster to 14 warbands. Each comes with its full hero and henchmen list, equipment options, and special rules.

title: Built for Tablet & Desktop
description: On a bigger screen the app now uses a left sidebar instead of the bottom tab bar, and keeps the content in a comfortable reading column rather than stretching across the whole window. Phones are unchanged.

title: See When a Warrior Earns an Advance
description: Hero and henchmen screens now show how much Experience is left until the next advance, and say "Ready for an advance!" when one is due. The thresholds were read straight off the official roster sheet's Experience track.

title: Clearer Navigation
description: The bottom tabs now use icons — a home, three warriors for Warbands, crossed swords for Battle, a coin for Trading, and a map for Campaign — so the labels stop crowding each other on narrow phones.

title: Weapons, Armour & More Rules
description: Added the Weapons & Armour and Miscellaneous Equipment chapters to the Rules Reference, plus the Underdog experience bonus table. Fixed every rule's page citation to match the real rulebook, and reordered everything to follow its actual chapter structure. Warbands, Trading, and Campaign each got a "Rules" toggle showing just what's relevant there, and a new Skills tab lists every skill.

title: Rules Reference & Offline Verification
description: Added a full searchable, offline Rules Reference covering Characteristics, Movement, Shooting, Close Combat, Leadership & Psychology, Magic, the Post-Battle Sequence, Trading, Skills, Injuries, Scenarios, warband-specific rules, and Border Town Burning. Verified the app genuinely works with no network connection once it's been opened once, and polished the "Add to Home Screen" experience on iOS.

title: Pre-Battle, During-Battle & a Real Skills System
description: Added a Pre-Battle setup step (pick or randomly roll a scenario, note your opponent) and a During-Battle tracker (turn counter, event log, quick roster reference for either side). Built a proper skills system with prerequisite checking, wired into both the roster screens and the Post-Battle Wizard.

title: Dice Rolls for Post-Battle & Trading
description: Added real roll buttons for Serious Injuries, Henchmen casualties, Hired Sword fate, Advances, and Rare item purchases — no more needing physical dice for the app to track.

title: Home Dashboard
description: Added a Home tab summarizing your campaign and all your warbands at a glance, and cleaned up the bottom navigation so it stops crowding as more tabs get added.

title: Campaign Log
description: Added a screen to track your campaign's battle history and, if you're using Border Town Burning, each warband's chosen objective and progress.

title: Direct Equipment Purchases
description: You can now buy equipment straight from a Hero, Hired Sword, or Henchmen Group's own detail screen, instead of always routing through the Trading Post.

title: Trading Post
description: Added buying Common and Rare equipment (including the Rare item availability roll) and selling gear back from the treasury.

title: Post-Battle Wizard
description: Added the guided 8-step post-battle sequence — injuries, experience, advances, dead models, income, upkeep — with a staged summary and undo, plus all 9 playable warband types.

title: Warband Roster Management
description: Added the ability to create a warband and manage its roster: Heroes, Henchmen Groups, and Hired Swords, with stats, XP, skills, and injuries.

title: First Release
description: Scaffolded the app and populated the core game data: warbands, equipment, skills, injuries, and advance tables, sourced from the rulebook.
